question: Which of the following products is formed on complete combustion of hydrocarbons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO₂ and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• On the **complete combustion of hydrocarbons**, the primary products formed are **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** and **water (H₂O)**. This process occurs when there is a sufficient supply of oxygen.
 
• Hydrocarbons consist of **carbon (C)** and **hydrogen (H)**. During complete combustion, carbon reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide (CO₂), and hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form water (H₂O).
 
• The general equation for the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon is: CₓHy + (x + y/4)O₂ → xCO₂ + (y/2)H₂O.
